properties.areaDesc: Okaloosa, FL; Santa Rosa, FL
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 5 at 4:47AM CDT until October 5 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southern Okaloosa County in northwestern Florida...
Southern Santa Rosa County in northwestern Florida...

* WHEN...Until 700 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 447 AM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Minor flooding is already
occurring in the advisory area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Wright, Fort Walton Beach, Niceville, Destin, Eglin AFB, Pace,
Valparaiso, Gulf Breeze, Mary Esther, Bagdad, Ocean City, Lake
Lorraine, Oriole Beach, Navarre, Shalimar, Cinco Bayou, Navarre
Beach, Pea Ridge, Floridatown and Wynnehaven Beach.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL 7 AM CDT THIS MORNING

properties.areaDesc: Death Valley National Park
properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued October 5 at 2:46AM PDT until October 9 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with high temperatures near 110
degrees and overnight lows only getting down to around 85 degrees.
This will yield at least major heat risk, impacting anyone without
adequate cooling and hydration.

* WHERE...Elevations in Death Valley National Park below 2000 feet.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

NWSheadline: EXTREME HEAT WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 8 PM PDT FRIDAY

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 5 at 5:24AM EDT until October 5 at 8:30AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Coffee County in southeastern Alabama...
Northwestern Dale County in southeastern Alabama...

* WHEN...Until 730 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 424 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 3 and 6 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Elba, Fort Rucker, Enterprise, Ozark, New Brockton, Ariton, Lee,
Tabernacle, Eanon, Mixons Crossroads, Camp Alaflo Bsa, Java,
Clintonville, Victoria, Woodland Grove Church, Greater Salem
Church, Frisco, Shell Army Field, Roeton and Arcus.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 730 AM CDT THIS MORNING
